subject: SLA tiered onramp & lead-time hedging for private GPU pools

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial MAP ask + lead-time constraints for private pool

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the product demo yesterday — the latency profile and predictable billing model look promising. Procurement asked me to get a mutual action plan (MAP) that spells out: evaluation milestones, acceptance criteria for Dedicated vs Private (we're leaning Private), and realistic lead times for GPU procurement and provisioning.

Key constraints on our side:
- We have a hard deadline to begin production experiments by 2027-01-15.
- Hardware team prefers H100-class or equivalent; supply team warned of 20–28 week lead times for certain SKUs.
- Security team needs SOC 2 artifacts and a network diagram before infra access.

Can you share a MAP + recommended hedging strategy for lead-time risk (e.g., staggered tranches, fallback to hosted/dedicated)? Also send any template checklists you use for private onramp.

Liam
Procurement | HexaBio

Hi Liam — appreciated the discussion.

High level: we can structure a MAP that lets HexaBio start with a hybrid approach to de-risk lead times: staged reservation (50% tranche to start), an interim Dedicated pool for scale-testing, and final migration to Private when hardware arrives. Below are proposed milestones and the files I attached: HexaMAP-v1.3.pdf (MAP draft), gpu-sku-leadtimes-2026Q3.xlsx (lead-time table), SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf.

Proposed milestone cadence (summary):
1) Evaluation kickoff — week 0: shared test dataset, baseline latency tests, security questionnaire completion (target 2 weeks)
2) Proof of concept — week 2–6: run 100k inference/day workload on Dedicated lane, validate throughput & cost buckets
3) Staged reservation commit — week 6–8: sign tranche 1 (50% compute) + PO for remaining timeline
4) Private onboarding & cutover — week 12–20 depending on SKU lead-time; final acceptance window aligned to your 2027-01-15 need

Questions for you:
- Do you have an internal preferred delivery cadence (all-in-one vs phased)?
- Target commit date for tranche 1? That will determine guaranteed lead time windows.

I looped in Karthik for sizing and Soojin for SOC2 gating.

Cheers,
Irene
Director, Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Attachments: HexaMAP-v1.3.pdf, gpu-sku-leadtimes-2026Q3.xlsx, SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf

Subject: Re: Initial MAP ask + lead-time constraints for private pool

Irene / Liam — quick technical note on GPU pool sizing and hedging:

Assumptions from discovery:
- Target production QPS: 45 requests/sec average, 150 rps peak (p95 bursts)
- Model: 70B decoder-only, effective context window 2k tokens, KV cache utilization typical for chat workloads

Sizing recommendation (starter tranche):
- Tranche 1 (staging): 8 x A100-80GB equiv for Dedicated testing (economical and available within 4–6 weeks)
- Tranche 2 (private final): 32 x H100-class nodes (or 16 with dynamic slicing depending on SKU) to meet 150 rps with headroom and batching — lead-time 18–26 weeks for certain H100 SKUs

Hedging strategies:
- Staggered procurement: place a soft PO for tranche 2 within 2–4 weeks to lock lead-time window; convert to firm PO after acceptance of tranche 1.
- Mix-and-match hardware: accept a portion of equivalent newer-generation cards that have shorter lead times, combined with reserved capacity on Redwood Dedicated while remaining inventory arrives.
- Pre-provisioning: we can provision network and virtualization layers in Parallel (2–3 week lead) to shorten the private cutover once hardware arrives.

I'll attach a short workbook with back-of-envelope capacity curves (see gpu-sku-leadtimes-2026Q3.xlsx). Happy to jump on a sizing call.

— Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: gpu-sku-leadtimes-2026Q3.xlsx

Liam
